interactions_checked.interaction: Ibuprofen taken before aspirin can reduce antiplatelet effect; combined GI irritation risk

contraindications.reason: SGLT2‑i require eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m²; renal function not provided

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not supplied – assumed ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² for dapagliflozin eligibility; actual value must be measured before starting.
Liver function tests not provided – high‑intensity atorvastatin requires normal‑to‑moderately elevated LFTs; baseline LFTs should be obtained.
Serum potassium not available – needed before initiating or titrating ACE‑I, thiazide, or any future MRA.
Allergy status (especially aspirin, statin, ACE‑I) not documented – confirm no hypersensitivity before prescribing.
Urine leukocytes elevated – possible urinary infection; obtain urine culture and treat before adjusting ACE‑I dose.
treatment_summary: The plan adds guideline‑directed secondary prevention for stable coronary artery disease: low‑dose aspirin, high‑intensity atorvastatin, a cardio‑selective beta‑blocker (bisoprolol) and, pending renal function confirmation, dapagliflozin for additional cardiovascular risk reduction. Existing antihypertensive triple therapy (lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide) and diabetes therapy (metformin) are continued. NSAID use is limited to short courses with timing advice to preserve aspirin efficacy. All new agents are justified by NICE CG126/NG185, NG136 and NG106. Monitoring includes lipid profile at 12 weeks, renal function/electrolytes after ACE‑I and SGLT2‑i changes, blood pressure and heart rate after beta‑blocker initiation, and regular review of opioid use and anemia status. Non‑pharmacological measures (smoking cessation, diet, exercise, weight management) should be reinforced.
